facts.text: I have pain in my belly.
It spreads to my sides (my flanks).

facts.item: how long the belly pain and nausea have lasted
facts.text: The belly pain and the nausea started 6 days ago.
I've been constipated for a long time.
I've had some discomfort in my legs.
For the past week I've been taking anti-inflammatory painkillers (NSAIDs) for the discomfort in my legs.
I was recently treated for pneumonia.
I get short of breath when I exert myself.

facts.item: shortness of breath on exertion: course
facts.text: It has been gradually getting worse over the past year.

facts.item: shortness of breath on exertion: limits my activities
facts.text: It doesn't stop me from doing my usual activities.
Eleven years ago I was told I have a heart murmur; it wasn't causing me any symptoms.
I've had my appendix taken out.
I've smoked a lot over the years: about 90 pack-years.

findings.name: cardiac examination
findings.result: Systolic ejection murmur, best heard in the aortic area.

findings.name: abdominal examination
findings.result: Flat, mildly tender abdomen; normal bowel sounds; no peritoneal signs.

findings.name: metabolic panel
findings.result: Creatinine 7.6 mg/dL (reference 0.4–1.3); urea 191 mg/dL (reference 10–50); potassium 5.6 mEq/L; other electrolytes normal.

findings.name: iron studies
findings.result: Iron profile consistent with iron-deficiency anemia.

findings.name: renal ultrasound
findings.result: Normal kidney size with parenchymal thickening.

findings.name: echocardiography
findings.result: Left atrial enlargement (47 mm); left ventricular ejection fraction 62%; septal thickness 17 mm; posterior wall thickness 14 mm; inferolateral hypokinesia; calcified aortic valve with severe stenosis (peak gradient 92 mmHg).

findings.name: renal biopsy
findings.result: Crescentic glomerulonephritis with medullary lymphomonocytic infiltration; of five glomeruli, four were sclerotic.

findings.name: viral serology
findings.result: HIV negative; hepatitis B negative; hepatitis C negative.

findings.name: ANCA testing
findings.result: p-ANCA positive at >1/80 (normal: nonreactive); myeloperoxidase antibody 120 U (normal <20).

gold.reasoning: 1. NSAID-induced acute interstitial nephritis — “initially considered as NSAID-induced acute interstitial nephritis ... but no improvement of renal function was observed.” 2. Severe aortic stenosis–related hemodynamic impairment — “Although it is a serious condition, we consider the AS to be a bystander lesion in the final event of this patient.” 3. Systemic lupus erythematosus — “Anti-nuclear antibody (ANA) ... and anti-DNA, were negative; complement determination was normal.” 4. Viral infections (HIV, hepatitis B, and C) — “Serologies for HIV, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C were negative.”
